title: Terms of Account: Opening and Funding a Personal Checking Account
content:
A Personal Checking account is opened awaiting its opening deposit, with a zero ledger balance, with the election on paying ATM and one-time debit card items into overdraft set to opted out, and with no overdraft protection source named.

**Entry conditions on the opening date.** The customer must satisfy the tier's entry gate on the opening date.

- *Age.* The customer's age in whole years on the opening date, computed from the date of birth held on the customer profile, must be at least the tier's youngest age to open and, where the tier sets one, no more than its oldest age to open. The date of birth on the profile is the authority; what the customer states about their age is not.
- *Relationship, for one tier.* For Private Client Checking the relationship balance on the opening date must be at least that tier's required relationship balance, read from the customer's own holdings before the account is opened.

**Funding.** The account becomes active on the business day its first deposit posts, provided that deposit is at least the tier's smallest first deposit. A smaller first deposit is returned to its source and does not activate the account.

**Lapse of an unfunded account.** An account still awaiting its opening deposit is closed as unfunded once 30 calendar days have passed after the account was opened. Count calendar days with the day after the opening date as day 1; the lapse is due when the frozen date is on or after the opening date plus 30 days. The opening date held on the account record is the anchor. No charge is taken on an unfunded closure.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical).** An account opened on a given date and still unfunded is not yet due to lapse on the 29th day counted from the day after opening. On the day that is the opening date plus 30 calendar days it is due, and it stays due on every later day, because the comparison is not-earlier-than and the boundary day itself satisfies it.
